title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the 'general digression' announced on the previous page. Its purpose is to measure how large the image of Π_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) is in Ẑ*·Ẑ (the affine group Ẑ(1) ⋊ Ẑ*). That image controls the Galois homomorphism (335) onto Gal(Q̃[(-1/2)^{1/∞}]/Q), where Q̃ = Q(μ_∞).

Setup. Take a base S (in practice S = Spec Q), an abelian group A (here A = Z) and a homomorphism ξ: A → G_m(S) = H^0(S, G_m) (here 1 ↦ -1/2). Equivalently, ξ is a morphism of S-group schemes A_S → G_{m,S} from the constant group.

Construction. Pull back the tower of Kummer sequences 1 → μ_n → G_m → G_m → 1 (the map being λ ↦ λ^n) along ξ. This gives a tower of extensions of étale S-group schemes, 1 → μ_n → E_n(ξ) → A_S → 1. Concretely, E_n(ξ) is the scheme of pairs (a, λ) with λ^n = ξ(a). Passing to the projective limit gives 1 → T_∞(G_{m,S}) = Ẑ(1) → E_∞(ξ) → A_S → 1.

Galois representation. For S connected with a geometric point s̄, the fibre E_∞(ξ)_s̄ is a profinite group. π_1(S, s̄) acts on it by automorphisms, giving (341): π_1(S, s̄) → Aut_{profinite groups}(E_∞(ξ)_s̄).

On the next page this action is seen to respect the extension structure. It is trivial on A and acts on Ẑ(1) through the cyclotomic character. It therefore lands in G, an extension of (part of) Ẑ* by Hom(A, Ẑ(1)), which is the affine group Ẑ(1) ⋊ Ẑ* when A = Z.

In modern terms, E_∞(ξ)_s̄ is essentially the ℓ-adic/adelic realization (Tate module) of the Deligne 1-motive [A → G_m]. The resulting representation is classical Kummer theory: its restriction to Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)) is the Kummer cocycle of the elements ξ(a). For ξ(1) = -1/2 it describes the field Q(μ_∞, (-1/2)^{1/∞}). In Grothendieck's context this seems to concern the Galois action on tangential base points or paths of the projective line minus three points.
errors: Minor: E_∞(ξ) is a pro-étale (pro-finite étale over A_S) group scheme rather than étale. The E_n are étale only when n is invertible on S, which is automatic for S = Spec Q.
Equation numbering is duplicated: two equations are labelled (338) on the page (with crossings-out), an artifact of renumbering.

ideas.what: Pulling back the Kummer tower along ξ: A_S → G_m gives extensions of A by μ_n and, in the limit, by Ẑ(1). The Galois action on the fibre lands in Hom(A, Ẑ(1)) ⋊ Ẑ*.
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory / Tate module (ℓ-adic realization) of the 1-motive [A → G_m]; Kummer representation in the affine group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Kummer theory; formalized via Deligne's 1-motives (Hodge III, 1974); image questions studied by Ribet, Bashmakov and others
ideas.where_published: Kummer torsors appear in SGA 4 / SGA 4½ (Deligne). This specific digression is in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation.

ideas.what: The question of the size of the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) in Ẑ(1) ⋊ Ẑ* for the element -1/2
ideas.modern_name: Open-image problem for Kummer extensions Q(μ_∞, a^{1/∞})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hasse, Schinzel; Bashmakov, Ribet in general)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard set-up of Kummer theory for a homomorphism A → G_m(S), equivalent to the Tate module of a 1-motive. It contains no new result and serves as preparation for computing an image size that is classically known.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ_m(S)' should be read as 'G_m(S) = H^0(S, G_{m,S})'.
The page has two labels '(338)' (renumbered/crossed out); the Kummer-tower equation is likely meant as a separate number (e.g. 338 bis).
'Aut_{gr pr. finis}' means automorphisms as profinite groups ('groupes profinis').
In (340), 'T_∞(G_{m,S})' is correct; 'pt géom s̄ de S' reads correctly after the crossed-out 'pt'.
